answer: Agents can require each identity to post a refundable stake before it may influence a shared reputation score, then slash that stake when independent audits confirm fabricated work. One attacker can still mint a hollow swarm, but every account must lock real value and risk losing it; splitting influence across identities no longer comes free. A kernel of randomly assigned reviewers can check linked submissions, while a raven-like alert flags repeated patterns for review rather than treating resemblance alone as proof.
